sections.html:
Herriman sits in the southwest corner of Salt Lake County. The city went from 1,523 residents in 2000 to 55,144 in 2020 and an estimated 63,282 in July 2025, so most homes are fairly recent construction. Newer houses mean fewer old-house surprises, yet a house with a tenant, a title wrinkle, an unfinished basement apartment or deferred upkeep still tends to lose financed buyers.

Mail here goes through the Riverton Post Office at 12760 S 2080 W, because Herriman has no post office of its own. Double-check that closing paperwork carries the right mailing address. City Hall is at 5355 West Herriman Main Street and opens weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.

The county calendar for a Herriman parcel runs like this:

  • July 22: valuation notices go out by mail.
  • August 1 to September 15: the Board of Equalization hears appeals.
  • November 1: tax notices arrive.
  • November 30: payment deadline.
  • December 1: unpaid current-year taxes become delinquent.

Utah knocks 45% off the taxable value of a main residence, leaving 55% of market value on the bill. The break goes to owners who live in the house, so a home you have rented out may not qualify.

The Salt Lake County Recorder records the deed. The flat fee is $40, and no more than ten legal descriptions fit before extra charges apply. The document needs a notary acknowledgment and the tax serial number of each parcel. A title company handles all of this on a cash sale, so you will not stand in line at the recorder yourself. Ask the title company for the final recording cost when you receive the settlement figures, and keep a copy of the recorded deed for your files.

Herriman City runs its own water department, and other services come from separate providers. A list like this helps when you transfer accounts at closing.

  • Water: the city bills around the 10th of each month, payment is due at month end, and a late charge of 1.5% starts on the second day after the due date.
  • Garbage: Wasatch Front Waste and Recycling.
  • Sewer: Jordan Basin Improvement District.
  • Fire: Unified Fire.
  • Schools: Jordan School District.

Opening a new water account costs a $200 deposit, refunded after 24 months if there are no more than two late payments. Buyers sometimes ask whether the current account is in good standing, so hold on to recent bills.

sections.h2: Does secondary water affect a sale?
sections.html:
Secondary water is a separate pressurized irrigation line for lawns and gardens, supplied by the Herriman City Water Department. It usually runs from early May to mid-October, then shuts down in stages.

To hook up, the homeowner has the sprinkler connection inspected, provides a backflow test report if the yard also draws culinary water, and asks the city to set a secondary meter. The city installs the meter. A filter is a good idea, since the water is filtered only to 200 microns.

If your yard still runs on culinary water, or the connection never passed inspection, expect a buyer or inspector to ask. It is an easy fix before closing, and clean records avoid a delay.

Herriman permits an internal accessory dwelling unit, called an I-ADU, only inside a single-family home, with one accessory unit per lot. Someone from the owner's household must be living on site, in the main house or in the unit.

  • The unit needs its own exterior entrance with a hard-surface walkway.
  • The application review fee is $559, plus a building permit fee that varies with the area remodeled.
  • Plan review takes about 7 to 14 business days.
  • The owner signs a notarized affidavit, which is recorded with the County Recorder.
  • After a passed inspection and an approval letter, the owner needs a business license before renting.

Unpermitted work can be opened up for inspection, which means pulling out finishes such as drywall and insulation. A basement apartment built without paperwork carries that cost, so factor it in before you list.

Exposed mountains, dry brush and open fields make Herriman fire-prone, and a 2010 blaze that started during a National Guard exercise at nearby Camp Williams burned about 3,500 acres. Utah's House Bill 48 of 2025 produced a statewide map that scores buildings from 1 (lowest) to 8 (highest) for wildfire exposure. Owners in the high-risk group may face an annual state fee once the program begins. Look your address up at wildfirerisk.utah.gov and see the score before a buyer does.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Herriman?
sections.html:
Because no bank is lending, the schedule hangs on title work alone.

  1. Tell us the address and the basics of the house.
  2. We study the property and recent nearby sales.
  3. You weigh the offer and answer yes or no.
  4. The title company checks the record and agrees a closing day with you.
  5. Once the deed is on record, your proceeds are released.

Lenders balk at an unfinished I-ADU, a secondary water problem or a late tax bill. We take the house as it is and settle those items at the closing table.

The offer comes after we look at the house and the sales around it, and you can say no without owing anything. If you accept, the title company orders the title search, confirms what is owed on the property and schedules signing. You sign, the deed is recorded, and the money is sent to you. There are no showings, no open houses and no buyer inspection requests to answer, and the house does not need to be cleaned out or repaired first.

A cash sale also removes the wait for a buyer's financing, which is the step most likely to fall through on a house with an unfinished basement or a utility question hanging over it. You pick the closing window, so the move can happen when your family needs it.

sections.h2: Before you sell: a short checklist
sections.html: Look up your tax status on the county calendar above and confirm nothing is delinquent. Find the permit paperwork for any finished basement. Note whether the yard is on secondary water and whether the connection passed inspection. Keep the last few water bills handy and decide where closing documents should be mailed, and who in the household needs to sign, given that Riverton handles the post. With those four items in hand, a title company can usually move quickly once you accept an offer.

faqs.a: Salt Lake County. The county assessor, treasurer and recorder handle your parcel.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Herriman?
faqs.a: November 30. Unpaid taxes are delinquent from December 1.

faqs.q: Can I rent out a basement apartment in Herriman?
faqs.a: Yes, if the home is a single-family house and the owner lives on the property. You need an I-ADU permit, a notarized affidavit recorded with the county, a passed final inspection and a business license before renting.
Jordan School District. The city has two high schools, Herriman High and Mountain Ridge High.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: The flat recording fee is $40, plus $2 for each legal description beyond ten. The document needs a notary acknowledgment and the tax serial number of each parcel.
